metadata.description: Curated high-value Italian gotchas — the little rules learners trip on most. Seeded into a learner's personal tricks-db via `tricks.py seed`; their own session-learned tricks accumulate alongside these.

tricks.rule: in for countries/regions, a for cities/towns
da = at someone's place / since / by
examples: Abito qui da due anni (for two years)

tricks.rule: Country vs nationality: Svizzera (the country, f.) vs svizzero (a Swiss person / adj.)
Common false friends: parenti = relatives (not parents → genitori); libreria = bookshop (library → biblioteca); fattoria = farm (factory → fabbrica); morbido = soft (not morbid)
essere vs stare: essere = identity/permanent; stare = state/how you are + location idioms
sapere vs conoscere: sapere = know a fact / know how to; conoscere = be acquainted with a person/place
examples: So nuotare (I know how to swim)

tricks.rule: piacere agrees with the thing liked, not the person: mi piace (sing.) / mi piacciono (pl.)
molto is invariable as an adverb ('very'), but agrees as an adjective ('much/many')
Watch gender traps: il problema / il tema / il programma are masculine despite -a; la mano is feminine despite -o
Double negative is required: non + niente/mai/nessuno
c'è (there is) vs ci sono (there are)
c/g are soft before e/i (ciao, gelato), hard before a/o/u (casa, gatto); che/chi and ghe/ghi restore the hard sound
Double consonants are held longer and change meaning
